objective: Close the same y+ restart-rename blindness in the mega-batch y+ gate that was just found and fixed in the bump collector, or show it cannot fire there
rationale: Found 2026-08-02 while fixing the bump ladder's own collector, and reported rather than edited because the mega-batch workflow is a shared module whose tests were red from another well's in-flight work at the time. OpenFOAM renames a function object's output by appending the restart time when the file already exists on a restart. The lab already knows this for the coefficient history, and the bump ladder's stitcher handles it for the force histories; the TMR verification workflow reads both the coefficient files and the wall-shear files through wildcards and so is safe. The one function object nobody wildcarded is y+. In the bump ladder this published the medium rung's y+ from iteration 5,000 beside a Cd from iteration 16,000, recovered only by reading the renamed, time-suffixed y+ file that sat beside a header-only original; the correction moved the numbers by 0.002 to 0.02 percent, small in magnitude and not in kind. The mega-batch collector sorts a recursive glob for the bare y+ filename and feeds the last match straight into its y+ gate, which raises when it fails, so this is a GATE reading a possibly stale value rather than a reported number. Two things make it latent rather than armed, and both need checking rather than assuming: a single-run case never triggers the rename, and the sort is over path strings so directories sort lexically while they are named for a run's start time in any case. The question is whether any mega-batch row has ever been restarted, and the ledger can answer it.
gate: Either the y+ read in mega_batch is made to select by the Time written inside the file across yPlus*.dat, matching the fix now in the bump collector, or the ledger is shown to contain no restarted row and the finding is recorded as latent with the evidence that it cannot currently fire
cost_basis: estimate; a read over the existing ledger plus at most a few lines of collection code and its test. No solver. The equivalent fix in the bump collector took no compute at all
expected_knowledge_gain: A gate that raises on a value it may have read from the wrong iteration is worse than a reported number that is wrong, because it decides rather than informs
citations: Bump ladder campaign record, NASA grids, section 6

TMR verification workflow, the wildcarded reads that are the counter-example
in_sample_verdict: Not applicable. Nothing is fitted, inverted or calibrated; this is a defect in how a measurement is read off disk.
outcome: Both halves of the gate closed. The mega-batch y+ gate now selects its state by the Time written inside the file across the wildcarded y+ outputs, matching the bump collector's repair, with a regression test that builds the renamed-restart layout and proves the fresh state wins where the old read picked a header-only leftover. The retrospective found zero affected rows: all 52 Ahmed ledger rows are single-attempt, every attempt builds in a wiped case directory since the family's first commit, and the 17 surviving case directories hold no renamed file, no multi-run time directory and no header-only original. The finding was latent, never armed, and the ledger stands.
